title: BIDA Work Permit in Bangladesh: Expatriate Visa, Security Clearance & NBR Tax Rules
metaTitle: BIDA Work Permit in Bangladesh: Expatriate Visa Guide 2026
metaDescription: Complete legal guide to BIDA work permits in Bangladesh: E-visa requirements, security clearance, NBR tax compliance, and renewal rules for expats.
heroIntro: With expanding foreign direct investment, infrastructure mega-projects, and multinational corporate presence in Bangladesh, employing expatriate managers, specialized engineers, and technical consultants is common practice. However, foreign nationals cannot lawfully work or receive local compensation in Bangladesh on a tourist, business, or visitor visa. Working without a formal statutory work permit constitutes a severe breach of immigration and foreign exchange laws, exposing both the expatriate employee and the employer company to heavy financial penalties, deportation, and immigration blacklisting. For industrial and commercial sectors, work permits are primarily granted by the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) under the Prime Minister's Office, alongside the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority (BEPZA) for EPZ units. This legal guide by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court Advocate and corporate practitioner in Uttara and Dhaka, outlines the end-to-end statutory procedure for securing BIDA work permits, E-visas, security clearances, and NBR tax compliance.

quickAnswer.title: Quick Overview: How to Obtain a BIDA Work Permit in Bangladesh
quickAnswer.heading: Quick Overview: How to Obtain a BIDA Work Permit in Bangladesh
quickAnswer.text: To employ a foreign national in Bangladesh, the sponsoring company must first be registered with BIDA (or BEPZA/BHTPA). The process involves four sequential stages: (1) Sponsoring company applies for an Employment Visa Recommendation (E-Visa) through the BIDA One-Stop Service (OSS) portal; (2) The expatriate obtains the E-Visa from the Bangladesh Embassy abroad and enters Bangladesh; (3) Within fifteen (15) days of arrival, the company submits the formal Work Permit Application to BIDA, adhering to the statutory 1:5 local-to-expatriate employment ratio; and (4) BIDA forwards the file to the Security Services Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs and Special Branch (SB) for mandatory police security clearance. BIDA work permits are typically granted for one to two years initially and are renewable. Foreign employees must obtain a local e-TIN and submit annual income tax returns to the NBR.
highlights: Governing Authorities: Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA), BEPZA, Ministry of Home Affairs (Security Services Division), and NBR.
Mandatory Visa Category: Expatriates must enter on an 'E' (Employment) visa; working on a 'B' (Business) or 'T' (Tourist) visa is illegal.
Statutory Ratio: Companies must maintain a minimum employment ratio of 1 foreign employee for every 5 local Bangladeshi staff (1:5 for commercial, 1:20 for industrial).
Timeline: Submit work permit application within 15 days of the foreign national's arrival in Bangladesh via BIDA OSS portal.
Security Clearance: Mandatory verification by the Special Branch (SB) and National Security Intelligence (NSI) coordinated via Home Ministry.
NBR Tax Obligations: Expatriates are subject to Bangladeshi income tax on worldwide or local earnings under the Income Tax Act 2023.
Departure Requirement: Income Tax Clearance Certificate under Section 166 of Income Tax Act 2023 required before final departure.

sections.title: 1. Statutory Framework: BIDA, BEPZA & Immigration Laws
sections.content:
In Bangladesh, foreign nationals cannot engage in gainful employment without prior official authorization from the Government. The regulatory framework is anchored in the Foreigners Act 1946 (Act No. XXXI of 1946), the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority Act 2016 (Act No. XXXVI of 2016), and statutory guidelines formulated by the Security Services Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Different statutory bodies issue work permits based on the industrial location and corporate structure of the sponsoring enterprise:

  • BIDA (Bangladesh Investment Development Authority): Regulates private limited companies, foreign branch offices, liaison offices, and commercial establishments operating outside export processing zones across Bangladesh.
  • BEPZA (Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority): Governs foreign nationals employed within designated Export Processing Zones (EPZs) under the Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority Act 1980.
  • BHTPA (Bangladesh Hi-Tech Park Authority): Regulates expatriate technology personnel employed in government-notified software technology parks and hi-tech zones.
  • NGO Affairs Bureau (NGOAB): Governs foreign consultants and executives working with registered non-governmental organizations funded by foreign donations.

Engaging expatriates without statutory permission exposes companies to penal sanctions, corporate tax penalty assessments from the National Board of Revenue, and cancellation of foreign remittance permissions. For company incorporation guidance, examine our guide on registering a 100% foreign-owned company in Bangladesh.

sections.title: 2. Step 1: Securing the E-Visa Recommendation via BIDA OSS
sections.content:
A common error made by international corporations is sending foreign executives to Dhaka on a Business Visa (B-Visa) or Tourist Visa (T-Visa) with the expectation of converting it locally. Bangladeshi immigration laws strictly bar local visa status conversion. An expatriate destined for employment must arrive with an official Employment Visa ('E' Visa) stamped in their passport prior to departure.

The procedural workflow to secure an E-Visa is as follows:

  1. BIDA Company Registration: The employer entity in Bangladesh must be registered with BIDA and possess an active profile on the BIDA One-Stop Service (OSS) digital portal.
  2. Board Resolution & Appointment Letter: The company board passes a formal resolution approving the employment, detailing designation, salary structure, and necessity of specialized overseas skills.
  3. Submission of E-Visa Recommendation Application: The company submits an online application on the BIDA OSS platform, attaching the expatriate's academic credentials, resume, passport copy, company memorandum, and appointment contract.
  4. Issuance of BIDA Recommendation Letter: Upon scrutiny, BIDA issues a formal Visa Recommendation Letter addressed to the relevant Bangladesh Embassy, High Commission, or Consulate abroad.
  5. Consular Visa Stamping: The expatriate presents the BIDA recommendation letter along with their passport to the designated Bangladesh mission abroad, which stamps the initial 3-month Employment ('E') Visa.

sections.title: 3. Step 2: Work Permit Filing & 15-Day Post-Arrival Rule
sections.content:
Upon touchdown at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (HSIA) or another international port of entry on a valid E-Visa, a strict statutory deadline begins. Under BIDA regulatory guidelines, the sponsoring employer must submit the formal online application for a Work Permit within fifteen (15) calendar days of the expatriate's physical arrival in Bangladesh.

The application packet submitted via the BIDA OSS platform must incorporate:

  • Copy of the stamped E-Visa and immigration entry seal showing the exact arrival date.
  • Certified copies of the employer company's BIDA Registration Certificate, RJSC Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, and current Trade License.
  • Detailed curriculum vitae, professional certificates, and university degrees of the expatriate (authenticated by relevant authorities if requested).
  • Copy of employment advertisement published in at least two widely circulated Bangladeshi national daily newspapers, demonstrating that qualified local candidates were unavailable.
  • Complete list of all local and foreign personnel currently employed by the enterprise, verifying adherence to statutory staffing ratios.

Submitting the work permit application after the 15-day window incurs daily administrative delay fines and can lead to immediate rejection by the BIDA Scrutiny Committee.

sections.title: 4. The 1:5 and 1:20 Local Employment Ratio Rules
sections.content:
Need legal assistance with BIDA work permits or expatriate visas? Contact our corporate immigration desk on WhatsApp at +880 1955-802007. We provide complete document vetting and government liaison.

To preserve domestic employment opportunities, the Government of Bangladesh enforces mandatory staffing ratios that companies must satisfy before work permits are sanctioned:

  • Commercial & Service Sector Companies (1:5 Ratio): For commercial offices, software firms, consulting agencies, branch offices, and liaison offices, the company must employ at least five (5) full-time Bangladeshi personnel for every one (1) expatriate employee.
  • Industrial & Manufacturing Enterprises (1:20 Ratio): For manufacturing plants, factories, and industrial facilities, the sponsoring entity must maintain an employment ratio of at least twenty (20) Bangladeshi workers for every one (1) foreign national.

The sponsoring enterprise must substantiate these ratios by submitting payroll sheets, bank salary transfer records, and employee e-TIN certificates. Top corporate executive appointments (such as Managing Director or Chief Executive Officer of a 100% foreign-owned subsidiary) may qualify for specialized consideration, but overall ratio thresholds remain strictly enforced during subsequent permit renewals.

sections.title: 6. Security Clearance: Home Ministry & Special Branch (SB) Vetting
sections.content:
Issuance of the physical BIDA work permit is conditional upon obtaining formal security clearance from the Government of Bangladesh. Upon granting provisional approval, BIDA automatically transmits the file to the Security Services Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The security verification process unfolds through two intelligence channels:

  1. Special Branch (SB) Verification: Officers from the Special Branch of Police visit the employer's registered commercial premises to verify physical operations, examine company books, interview local directors, and verify the foreign national's physical residence and passport credentials.
  2. National Security Intelligence (NSI) Review: State intelligence agencies review international background databases, travel histories, and INTERPOL records to ensure the individual poses no security, financial, or political risks.

Security clearance is typically concluded within 45 to 60 days. If an adverse report is rendered due to administrative errors or mistaken identity, the sponsoring enterprise must promptly submit a formal review petition accompanied by verified credentials. In arbitrary rejection cases, remedies lie before the High Court Division under Article 102. See our guide on travel bans and airport offloading in Bangladesh.

sections.title: 7. Expatriate Income Tax Compliance Under Income Tax Act 2023
sections.content:
A critical statutory obligation accompanying any work permit in Bangladesh is personal income taxation administered by the National Board of Revenue (NBR) under the Income Tax Act 2023 (Act No. XII of 2023).

Key statutory tax mandates include:

  • Mandatory e-TIN Registration: Within thirty (30) days of receiving the work permit, the expatriate employee must register for a 12-digit electronic Tax Identification Number (e-TIN) through the NBR digital portal.
  • Taxation Rates: Foreign nationals qualifying as non-residents are taxed at a flat rate of 30% on total Bangladeshi-sourced income without the personal basic exemption thresholds available to domestic taxpayers, unless beneficial double tax avoidance treaties (DTAA) apply.
  • Monthly Source Tax Deduction (TDS): Under Section 86 of the Income Tax Act 2023, the employer company must deduct tax at source on a monthly payroll basis and deposit it into the government exchequer via treasury e-chalans.
  • Tax Clearance Certificate for Final Departure: Under Section 166 of the Income Tax Act 2023, an expatriate cannot lawfully leave Bangladesh permanently upon completion of employment without obtaining a formal Tax Clearance Certificate from the competent Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT). Immigration authorities at international airports can prevent departure if tax clearances are unverified.

sections.title: 8. Renewal, Extension & Final Cancellation Procedures
sections.content:
Work permits are initially granted for a term of one to two years and require structured legal maintenance:

  1. Timely Renewal Application: The employer must file the work permit extension application through BIDA OSS at least thirty (30) to sixty (60) days prior to the expiration date of the current permit. Late applications trigger administrative penalties and risk visa lapses.
  2. Documentation for Extension: Submissions must include updated tax payment chalans, personal income tax returns, audited company accounts, proof of local training succession planning, and current staff ratio certifications.
  3. Maximum Cumulative Tenure: Under national policy, an expatriate employee is generally permitted to work in Bangladesh for a maximum cumulative period of five (5) years. Extensions beyond five years require exceptional justification demonstrating that specialized technical expertise remains unavailable in the domestic labor force.
  4. Final Cancellation & Surrender: When the employment contract concludes, the company must submit a formal Work Permit Cancellation Application to BIDA, surrender the permit, obtain NBR tax clearance under Section 166, and apply to the Department of Immigration & Passports (DIP) for an exit permit.

sections.title: 9. Illustrative Scenario: Regularizing an Expatriate Technical Director
sections.content:
Illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed): A European industrial manufacturing joint venture based in the Gazipur industrial belt appointed a German national as Chief Technical Officer to oversee high-precision automation installation. The executive entered Dhaka on a short-term 90-day business visa, but the enterprise failed to file for an employment visa recommendation prior to arrival. As the 90-day visa neared expiry, commercial operations faced severe disruption, and the local company faced penalties from the Directorate of Registration and BIDA.

The company engaged Advocate Md. Shah Alam's chamber to structure a lawful resolution:

  1. Audited the corporate structure and verified that the joint venture maintained a compliant 1:22 local-to-foreign staffing ratio.
  2. Advised the executive to complete a scheduled business trip to Singapore, during which our chamber filed an emergency E-Visa Recommendation Application on the BIDA OSS portal with supporting board resolutions and engineering credentials.
  3. Coordinated with BIDA and secured the official E-Visa Recommendation Letter within five working days, transmitting it to the Bangladesh High Commission in Singapore, which stamped the official Employment ('E') Visa.
  4. Upon the executive's return to Dhaka, filed the formal BIDA Work Permit Application within eight days, facilitating physical Special Branch premises verification.
  5. Assisted the executive in obtaining an e-TIN, structuring monthly payroll tax deductions under the Income Tax Act 2023, and successfully securing the final 2-year BIDA work permit without disruption to the industrial plant.

faqs.question: Can a foreign national work in Bangladesh on a Business or Tourist visa?
faqs.answer: No. Working or receiving compensation on a Tourist (T) or Business (B) visa is strictly illegal under the Foreigners Act 1946. Expatriates must enter on an Employment (E) visa recommended by BIDA or BEPZA.

faqs.question: What is the minimum local-to-foreign employee ratio required by BIDA?
faqs.answer: BIDA mandates a minimum ratio of 1 foreign employee for every 5 Bangladeshi employees (1:5) in commercial and consulting firms, and 1 foreign employee for every 20 local employees (1:20) in industrial manufacturing enterprises.

faqs.question: How long does it take to obtain a BIDA work permit in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The initial BIDA work permit approval typically takes 2 to 4 weeks following application. Full security clearance from the Home Ministry and Special Branch (SB) generally takes an additional 45 to 60 days.

faqs.question: What happens if a work permit application is not filed within 15 days of arrival?
faqs.answer: Failing to submit the application within 15 days of entering on an E-visa violates BIDA guidelines, incurring administrative delay fines and jeopardizing visa extension before the Department of Immigration & Passports.

faqs.question: What is the personal income tax rate for foreign expatriates in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Non-resident foreign employees are subject to a flat income tax rate of 30% on total Bangladeshi-sourced compensation under the Income Tax Act 2023, subject to applicable Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA).

faqs.question: Can an expatriate transfer employment to another company in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the expatriate must first obtain a formal No Objection Certificate (NOC) and tax clearance from the original employer, cancel the existing work permit, and secure a fresh work permit sponsored by the new entity.

faqs.question: What is a Section 166 Tax Clearance Certificate for departing expatriates?
faqs.answer: Under Section 166 of the Income Tax Act 2023, an expatriate permanently departing Bangladesh must obtain an official certificate from the NBR confirming all taxes have been fully satisfied before airport immigration permits exit.

faqs.question: What is the maximum cumulative period an expatriate can work in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The standard maximum cumulative term is five (5) years. Extensions beyond five years are granted only under exceptional circumstances where specialized technical skills remain demonstrably unavailable in the local labor market.
